findings.where: Where we're starting: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), each with its 'Best hostels ›' line
findings.fault: The cards look clickable but do nothing. Each one is a white card with a raised shadow, a hover rule, a chevron and 'Best hostels' in link colour, yet none of them is a link (parts p8–p10 are static). Sending visitors to the destination guides is one of this page's three jobs, so the page cannot do it. Both 'Explore destinations' and the nav's 'Destinations' scroll to this dead end.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker deciding between Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok taps 'Best hostels ›' and nothing happens. They are left with no guide, and probably the sense that the site is broken.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank' and footer 'How we rank', 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: Every one of these links leads back to this same page. The ranking method is the claim the hero makes ('ranks hostels on merit alone'), but the link meant to prove it goes nowhere, and so do the legal and report links.
findings.who_objects: A doubtful backpacker clicks 'How we rank' to see whether 'merit alone' is real, and the page just reloads. The claim now looks hollow, and the dead Privacy and Terms links look like a placeholder site.

findings.where: Where we're starting: the section heading
findings.fault: The section heading is set far larger than anything in the hero, larger even than the wordmark headline, and on desktop it takes two whole lines and most of a screen. A label for three small cards becomes the loudest thing on the page. The hero's claim and its call to action look minor beside it, and the cards are pushed below the first screen.
findings.who_objects: The visitor's eye lands on 'Where we're starting' before the product's promise or the sign-up, and they must scroll past a wall of type to reach the destinations.

findings.where: Destination cards: the card titles and the BALI / LOMBOK eyebrows
findings.fault: The place names and island labels are set in a typewriter-style monospace font. The rest of the page uses Quicksand and Nunito Sans, so the cards look like unstyled code or a broken font, not part of the brand.
findings.who_objects: The visitor sees these cards as half-finished or broken, right at the point where they choose where to go. The founder would object as well: card titles are set in Quicksand 600.

findings.where: Destination cards: the borders and shadow
findings.fault: Each card has a thick purple border, a colour found nowhere else in the brand, and a heavy soft shadow at rest. The result looks like a different site's widget dropped onto the sand ground.
findings.who_objects: The founder would object: the rules file allows no purple, cards take a thin sand-border, and nothing rests under a heavy shadow. The visitor would notice a jarring, off-brand block.

findings.where: Hero: the headline block (small line 'The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.' above the large 'MantaHostels')
findings.fault: The largest type in the hero is just the brand name, which the nav already shows. The actual promise is a small, vague line above it ('the better way'). The specific claim, merit-only ranking with booking direct or through your usual site, sits in small body text. The loudest slot carries no claim at all.
findings.who_objects: A first-time backpacker scanning for five seconds learns the name twice but not why this beats the booking site they already use.

findings.where: Hero: the coral 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news' button
findings.fault: The only sign-up is a mailto link with the whole address in its label. It wraps onto two lines on a phone, and it opens a mail app with an empty message. Nothing says what to write, what they will receive, how often, or when launch is.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone, possibly with no mail app set up, has to compose an email to a stranger with no idea what they are signing up for. Many will not bother.

findings.where: Hero: the coral button and the 'Explore destinations' button
findings.fault: The two buttons share no shape language: one is a full pill, the other a square-cornered box with a thin outline on turquoise. Neither uses the 8 px control radius of the house button style, so they look like they come from two kits.
findings.who_objects: The founder would object, since buttons take the 8 px control radius. The visitor sees a mismatched, unfinished hero.

findings.where: Footer tagline 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali'
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali only, while the destination cards right above it include Kuta Lombok.
findings.who_objects: A visitor planning Lombok cannot tell whether Lombok is covered. The contradiction makes the site look careless.

findings.fault: Each card holds only an island and a place name. There is no line on what the place is like (surf, nightlife, quiet) to help a first-timer choose which guide to open.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on their first trip who does not know Canggu from Uluwatu gets no help choosing which one to look at.

findings.fault: The two nav links are styled differently: 'How we rank' is underlined and 'Destinations' is not. That reads as if 'Destinations' were the current page, which it is not.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading the nav cannot tell which page they are on, or why one link looks different from the other.

findings.where: Whole page: who is behind it and when it launches
findings.fault: Apart from the first name in the email address, nothing says who runs MantaHostels or when it will launch. A pre-launch product asking for contact details gives no person and no date.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker asked to send their email to an unknown pre-launch site wants to know someone real is behind it and whether it will be ready before their trip.
